description: Three-panel composite of bright-field TEM micrographs, each with a selected-area diffraction pattern (SADP) inset; the group is dominated by TEM imaging but every panel carries its own diffraction inset. (a) 0Cr, (b) 3Cr and (c) 6Cr steel strips after cold rolling with 20% reduction. Each micrograph carries a 500 nm scale bar at lower right and an orange double-headed arrow labelled {111} marking the separation between planar slip bands; each SADP inset is labelled [110] and shows a discrete crystalline spot pattern consistent with a single-crystal γ-austenite region viewed down the [110] zone axis. Panel (a) shows widely spaced, coarse parallel planar slip bands traversing the austenite with relatively clean areas between them; (b) shows markedly denser, finer and more closely spaced {111} slip bands; (c) shows the densest set of parallel bands with heavily overlapping deformation contrast. Read in sequence, the panels show that increasing Cr content progressively refines the {111} planar slip band spacing in cold-rolled γ-austenite, which the citing text attributes to the stronger reinforcement effect after cold rolling. Numbers for spacing are not printed on the panels.

observations.observation: The figure is a three-panel set of bright-field TEM micrographs, one per steel strip, each containing a selected-area diffraction pattern inset in its upper-right corner.
Every panel carries a scale bar of 500 nm at the lower right.
Each SADP inset is annotated with the zone axis label [110] and shows a discrete spot pattern, consistent with diffraction from a single-crystal region.
In each panel an orange double-headed arrow labelled {111} spans the spacing between parallel planar slip bands.

The slip bands become progressively denser and more closely spaced from panel (a) to (b) to (c); panel (a) shows widely separated coarse bands, whereas panel (c) shows the finest, most heavily overlapping band set.
The caption states the three panels are γ-austenite microstructures of 0Cr (a), 3Cr (b) and 6Cr (c) steel strips after cold rolling with 20% reduction.
The citing text states the BF images and SADP were taken from the [110] zone axis of the γ-austenite in the three CR20% steel strips.
The citing text states that {111} planar slip bands are present in the austenite of the CR20% steel strips.
The citing text states the measured average slip band spacing is 371 ± 47 nm for 0Cr, 100 ± 15 nm for 3Cr and 45 ± 13 nm for 6Cr, measured in at least three regions per specimen.
The citing text states the difference in slip band spacing is responsible for the difference in reinforcement effect, with smaller slip band spacing giving stronger reinforcement after cold rolling.
The citing text states that cold rolling leaves a large number of dislocations and slip bands in the steel strips, and that subsequent annealing does not eliminate them.

subfigures.description: BF TEM micrograph of CR20% 0Cr steel strip with a [110] SADP inset (upper right) and a 500 nm scale bar (lower right); an orange double-headed arrow labelled {111} spans the spacing between widely separated parallel planar slip bands in the γ-austenite.

BF TEM micrograph of CR20% 3Cr steel strip with a [110] SADP inset and a 500 nm scale bar; the {111} planar slip bands are noticeably denser and more closely spaced than in (a), with the orange {111} arrow marking the band separation.

BF TEM micrograph of CR20% 6Cr steel strip with a [110] SADP inset and a 500 nm scale bar; heavily deformed austenite showing the finest, most densely spaced parallel {111} slip bands of the three panels, indicated by the orange {111} arrow.
